_purpose: Asset/render half of DoD item 5 for the two blue-seed CONTACT-OBJECT outputs: B06 invincibility (ctor 0x25) and B08 bubble (ctor 0x1F). Covers (1) what indexes contact metadata table A 0x80079E30 and what its rows mean, (2) the decode of fcn.800593E8, (3) the renderer that walks the 64 x 0x38 contact array at 0x800B0D18, (4) whether these two pickups carry any per-level asset dependency of their own.
_scope_note: This file ADDS to, and does not restate, analysis/phase4_b06_b08_powerups.json 'production_chain'. Everything there is taken as given (contact_alloc = 0x80059E44, a3 = ctor, 0x10(sp) stack arg reloaded as 0x40(sp), metaB = 0x8007941C stride 0x14 by ctor, metaB+0x00 = action id, walker dispatch 0x8001B570[action-2]).

correction_to_the_brief.claim_in_brief: these are CONTACT OBJECTS, so the 0x80096B98 kind->descriptor Canon does NOT apply to them
correction_to_the_brief.finding: REFUTED. The contact renderer uses the SAME table 0x80096B98 and the SAME 0xC+ byte descriptor structs as type-0x3f pickups. The difference is only the INDEX: type-0x3f pickups index it by the record's kind byte; contact objects index it by contact-record +0x20, which is the metaB ACTION ID.
correction_to_the_brief.consequence: rec+0x20 is a DOUBLE-DUTY index: it selects both the behaviour handler (0x8001B570[action-2]) and the sprite descriptor (0x80096B98[action]). Verified live for both of our rows (see live_confirmation).
correction_to_the_brief.actionable_warning: The memory note 'pickup-render-kind-descriptor-table' lists 0x15-0x20, 0x25-0x28, 0x2E, 0x2F as 'have-descriptor-but-never-placed, safe to repurpose'. That is a type-0x3f-only statement. Descriptor indices 0x15, 0x19, 0x20 and 0x2E ARE consumed by contact objects (see descriptor_indices_consumed_by_contact_objects) and repurposing them would corrupt contact rendering. 0x25 is NOT among them, so the previously proven kind-0x25 mod is unaffected.

index_expression.measured: s0 = 0x80079E30 + a3 * 0x14, where a3 is RELOADED from 0x40(sp) at 0x80059E50 -- i.e. the caller's 5th argument at 0x10(sp), NOT the ctor.
disassembly: 0x80059E50  lw     a3, 0x40(sp)        ; a3 := caller 0x10(sp) (the ctor originally in a3 was already saved to s3 at 0x80059E4C)
0x80059EEC  addu   s0, s0, a3          ; s0 = a3*5
index_expression.so: table A IS simply indexed by the stack arg, stride 0x14. The brief's doubt is resolved.

why_row_3_is_all_zeros.meaning: NOT a contradiction and NOT an unused row. Word0 == 0 means all four selector nibbles are 0; selector 0 is the pass-through case in fcn.800593E8, which returns the row value unchanged. All four row values are 0, so record +0x0C/+0x10/+0x14/+0x18 are all set to 0 and NO random byte is consumed. Row 3 is the 'spawn perfectly still, zero scatter' profile -- exactly right for a stationary collectible token.
why_row_3_is_all_zeros.consistency_check: The B08 handler at 0x8005C6F0-0x8005C728 passes 3, and the B08 token is the one that hovers in place; the B06 handler at 0x8005C7BC-0x8005C800 passes 6, whose row gives a wide XZ scatter and a strong upward Y impulse.

row_layout.+0x00: u32 selector pack. Only the low 16 bits are used, as four nibbles: (w>>12)&0xF -> field0, (w>>8)&0xF -> field1, (w>>4)&0xF -> field2, w&0xF -> field3.
row_layout.+0x04: u32 value for field0 -> contact record +0x0C
row_layout.+0x08: u32 value for field1 -> contact record +0x10
row_layout.+0x0C: u32 value for field2 -> contact record +0x14
row_layout.+0x10: u32 value for field3 -> contact record +0x18

result_formulas.+0x10: ((r1 & 0x143F) - 0x140) << 3 -> r1 is a BYTE so r1 & 0x143F == r1 & 0x3F, giving [-2560 .. -2056] (large negative)

task1_table_A_0x80079E30.row_count: UNRESOLVED. Row index 24 was observed live, so >= 25 rows exist. The table starts at 0x80079E30; the next known named datum in the vault is the seed pair table at 0x8007A448, which would cap it at 78 rows. Not proven.
task1_table_A_0x80079E30.field_semantics_of_the_four_outputs: INFERRED, NOT PROVEN. The pattern (two symmetric components + one biased component + one literal) is consistent with velocity X / velocity Y / velocity Z / a fourth scalar, and +Y is down in this engine so row 6's large negative field1 is an upward launch. This was NOT verified because the per-action walker handler mutates +0x0C..+0x18 every frame (a live B06 record 11 frames old already had +0x10 = -720, outside row 6's spawn range, and +0x1C had changed from -1 to 228).

task2_fcn_800593E8.status: SOLVED (MEASURED statically, verified live 24/24 exact matches)
task2_fcn_800593E8.extent: 0x800593E8 .. 0x8005953B (jr ra at 0x80059534, delay slot 0x80059538 'addu v0, a1, zero')
task2_fcn_800593E8.signature: u32 f(u32 selector_nibble, u32 value) -- returns in v0
task2_fcn_800593E8.control_flow: a0 -= 1; if ((unsigned)a0 >= 6) fall through to the tail and RETURN value UNCHANGED. Otherwise jr [0x8001B778 + a0*4].
task2_fcn_800593E8.random_source: Every one of the six cases does the identical 4-instruction sequence: v1 = *(u32*)0x800822F4; *(u32*)0x800822F4 = v1 + 1; r = *(u8*)v1. So 0x800822F4 is a BYTE-STREAM CURSOR into a table of pre-generated random bytes (live value observed: 0x80017F53, i.e. it points INTO THE EXE TEXT -- the game reuses its own code image as a noise table). Selector 0 / >=7 consumes NOTHING.
task2_fcn_800593E8.note_on_shifts: the >>1 and >>4 are ARITHMETIC (sra), so a negative row value biases negative.
task2_fcn_800593E8.what_it_writes: Nothing. It is a pure value transform (apart from advancing the 0x800822F4 cursor). contact_alloc stores the four results into record +0x0C/+0x10/+0x14/+0x18.

live_verification.method: execute breakpoint at 0x80059F18 (after s0/s1/s2 are computed, before the four calls); read s0/s1/s2, the table-A row, and the next 4 bytes at *(0x800822F4); then debugger.runUntilAddress 0x80059F80 and read record +0x0C..+0x18; recompute the four values from the formulas above and compare.
live_verification.result: 24 consecutive hits, 24/24 EXACT matches on all four u32 outputs. Table-A row address decoded to index 24 every time; ctor decoded to 0x71 every time (proving the two indices are genuinely independent). Selector pattern exercised: [1,0,1,0] (case 1 and the pass-through).
live_verification.coverage_gap: cases 2,3,4,5,6 were NOT exercised live; they are static-only.

function.arguments: a0/a1/a2 = camera world X/Y/Z. At the call site a0 = *(s1) and a1/a2 come from scratchpad 0x1F800378 / 0x1F80037C.

archived_candidate_0x80014A70.verdict: VERIFIED, with a clarification. 0x80014A70 (`sw v1, 4(s7)`) IS inside this function -- it is the store of the primitive's colour+code word into POLY_FT4 offset +0x04. The function containing it, 0x80014844, is the contact-object renderer. The archived note pointed at the right code; 0x80014A70 is not itself 'the emitter' but one store within the per-object primitive build.

proof_it_is_this_array: 0x80014848  addi  t9, zero, 64          ; loop counter = 64 slots

sprite_not_mesh.verdict: SPRITES. Each drawn record emits exactly one 40-byte POLY_FT4 (textured 4-point polygon), screen-aligned.
evidence: primitive cursor s7 = *(0x8008249C); advanced by 40 (0x28) per emitted object at 0x80014A8C and written back at 0x80014AA8. sizeof(POLY_FT4) == 40.
field offsets written are exactly the POLY_FT4 layout: tag +0x00, rgb/code +0x04, XY0 +0x08, UV0/CLUT +0x0C, XY1 +0x10, UV1/TPAGE +0x14, XY2 +0x18, UV2 +0x1C, XY3 +0x20, UV3 +0x24.
the four screen XYs are built from only TWO transformed corners: XY0 = SXY0, XY3 = SXY1, XY1 = (SXY1.x, SXY0.y), XY2 = (SXY0.x, SXY1.y) -- an axis-aligned rectangle in SCREEN space.

the GTE rotation matrix RT is loaded ONCE before the loop to a constant (ctc2 6553 -> $0, ctc2 4096 -> $2, ctc2 4096 -> $4 = diag(1.6, 1.0, 1.0)) and never reloaded, so the quad corners are never rotated by the camera; only the TRANSLATION (TRX/TRY/TRZ) is per-object.
the record's own tint word (+0x34..+0x36) and GPU code byte (+0x37 = 0x2C or 0x2E) are copied straight into the primitive.

per_object_pipeline_measured.1_liveness: lbu t0, 0x22(t8); if 0 -> skip. NOTE: this is a BYTE load of the LOW byte of the 16-bit lifetime at +0x22.
per_object_pipeline_measured.2_draw_flag: lbu t1, 0x32(t8); t1 &= 0xFE; ... t1 += 1 only if the primitive is actually emitted; sb t1, 0x32(t8) at the end of every iteration. So record +0x32 bit0 == 'was drawn this frame'.
per_object_pipeline_measured.3_position: (rec+0x00, +0x04, +0x08) - (a0,a1,a2) then >> 5 arithmetic -> IR1/IR2/IR3; MVMVA (cop2 0x04BE012: op 0x12, sf=1, mx=1 (light matrix used as the view rotation), v=3 (IR), cv=3 (none)) -> MAC1/2/3 -> ctc2 into TRX/TRY/TRZ.
per_object_pipeline_measured.4_quad: VXY0 = (-(rec+0x28), -(rec+0x2A)), VXY1 = (+(rec+0x28), +(rec+0x2A)); VZ0/VZ1/VZ2 were zeroed before the loop; RTPT (cop2 0x0280030).
per_object_pipeline_measured.5_descriptor: lhu t2, 0x20(t8); if 0 -> skip (an action id of 0 is never drawn). desc = *(u32*)(0x80096B98 + action*4).
per_object_pipeline_measured.7_screen_cull: skip unless SXY0 or SXY1 is below 0x00F00000, and unless the low half of SXY0 or SXY1 is < 512.
per_object_pipeline_measured.8_ot_insert: bucket = (*(u32*)0x80082230) + *(u16*)(0x800A3390 + (s4 & ~1)); classic addPrim: prim.tag = *bucket + 0x09000000 (9 words follow); *bucket = prim & 0x00FFFFFF.
per_object_pipeline_measured.10_colour: prim+0x04 = *(u32*)(rec+0x34) = { R = rec+0x34, G = rec+0x35, B = rec+0x36, code = rec+0x37 }.

descriptor_struct.+0x00: u8 atlas/type tag (0x1C, 0x1D, 0x1E for the EXE-resident ones; 0x1D is the type-0x3f 'sprite pickup' value already in Canon). NOT read by this renderer.
descriptor_struct.+0x02: u8 width-1 in texels (added to u to give u1/u3)
descriptor_struct.+0x03: u8 height-1 in texels (added to v to give v2/v3)
descriptor_struct.+0x04: u16 TPAGE -- ZERO IN THE EXE IMAGE, written at runtime
descriptor_struct.+0x06: u16 CLUT id -- ZERO IN THE EXE IMAGE, written at runtime
descriptor_struct.+0x08 + 2*n: u16 per-frame (u | v<<8); frame index comes from record +0x31

record_field_map_measured.+0x1C: s32 = -1 at spawn (walker overwrites it; purpose UNRESOLVED)
record_field_map_measured.+0x20: u16 ACTION ID = metaB+0x00. Indexes BOTH 0x8001B570[action-2] (behaviour) and 0x80096B98[action] (sprite descriptor).
record_field_map_measured.+0x22: s16 lifetime = metaB+0x02, or (rng&3) - (u16)metaB+0x04 scaled when metaB+0x04 is negative. Used as the slot-busy test in contact_alloc and (low byte only) as the renderer's liveness test.
record_field_map_measured.+0x30: u8 = metaB+0x07 (also used as a multiplier for +0x22 in the randomized-lifetime branch)
record_field_map_measured.+0x31: u8 = metaB+0x06 at spawn; SPRITE FRAME INDEX read by the renderer, advanced by the action handler
record_field_map_measured.+0x32: u8 = 0x20 at spawn; renderer clears bit0 each frame and sets it if the primitive was emitted
record_field_map_measured.+0x33: u8 flags = metaB+0x10. bit7 = slot occupied (contact_alloc's reuse test). bits 5-6 are ADDED INTO THE TPAGE, i.e. they are the GPU semi-transparency (ABR) field.
record_field_map_measured.+0x37: u8 GPU primitive code, set by contact_record_post_init 0x80024DDC: default 0x2C, changed to 0x2E unless (rec+0x33 & 0x60) == 0x60. 0x2C = opaque textured quad, 0x2E = SEMI-TRANSPARENT textured quad.

slot_allocation_measured.cursor: 0x8008234C (census name contact_alloc_cursor); pre-incremented, wrapped to 0 at 64
slot_allocation_measured.reuse_test: a slot is skipped (cursor advances again) only if (rec+0x33 & 0x80) != 0 AND (s16)rec+0x22 != 0; otherwise it is overwritten
slot_allocation_measured.second_allocator: 0x8005A0E0 is a longer-argument variant with the identical cursor/slot logic (t1..t3/t0 pulled from 0x30/0x34/0x38/0x3C(sp)); not used by the blue-plant path

B06_invincibility.behaviour_handler: 0x800588B0 (read from 0x8001B598 = 0x8001B570 + (0x0C-2)*4) -- matches the handler already recorded in phase4_b06_b08_powerups.json
B06_invincibility.tint_RGB: 0xFF / 0xC0 / 0x00 (gold; 0x80 is the neutral level, so this is a strong warm modulation)
B06_invincibility.sprite: 32 x 32, 4 UV frames at (0x40,0x80) (0x60,0x80) (0x40,0xA0) (0x60,0xA0) -- an animated 4-frame twinkle

B08_bubble.spawn_half_extent: 1 x 1 (so the visible size at spawn is sub-pixel; the on-screen size must be grown by handler 0x80058998 -- INFERRED, not decoded)
B08_bubble.sprite: 63 x 64, a SINGLE UV frame at (0x80,0x40)

live_confirmation.how: Replayed movies/B06_movie.json on the Interpreter instance (poll-only, no instrumentation) and scanned all 64 records each poll for an action id of 0x0C or 0x2E.

decoded_and_matched.+0x31: 1 (spawned 0 = metaB+0x06; advanced by the handler -> the 4-frame animation is real)
decoded_and_matched.+0x32: 0x21 -- bit0 SET, i.e. the billboard renderer DREW this record on this frame

task4_per_level_asset_dependency.status: SOLVED (MEASURED live across five level states)
task4_per_level_asset_dependency.short_answer: YES, but only a VRAM/CLUT REBINDING, not a distinct per-level file. Neither pickup needs any asset of its own beyond (a) the plant body model already recorded in phase4_b06_b08_powerups.json and (b) a common sprite bank that every level already loads. The sprite bitmaps and palettes are byte-identical in every level tested; only the VRAM page and CLUT slot they are placed at change.

measurements.descriptor_pointer_table_is_BSS: 0x80096B98 is above the EXE image end (0x80082800), so it does not exist in the file; it is built at load. An abstract-interpreter scan of every lui/ori/addiu-formed effective address in the whole resident text found TWENTY reads of 0x80096B98.. and ZERO writes, so the builder is either pointer-walking through a base the scan cannot fold, or lives in an overlay. See unresolved.

pointer_stability.0x80096B98[0x0C]: 0x80081EF8 in LEVEL01, LEVEL04, LEVEL06, LEVEL08, LEVEL13
pointer_stability.0x80096B98[0x2E]: 0x8008203C in LEVEL01, LEVEL04, LEVEL06, LEVEL08, LEVEL13
pointer_stability.conclusion: both descriptors are EXE-RESIDENT and their identity never changes per level

descriptor_body_static_vs_live.conclusion: ONLY +0x04 (tpage) and +0x06 (clut) are runtime-written. Geometry (w/h) and all UVs come from the EXE.

vram_content_is_identical.method: gpu.readVramRect over each sprite's exact texel rectangle, computed from that state's own tpage, then sha256
vram_content_is_identical.vram_addresses: B06 at (656,128) in LEVEL01/04/08/13 and (592,128) in LEVEL06; B08 at (736,64) and (672,64) respectively

palettes_are_identical.method: gpu.readVramRect of the 16-entry CLUT row at the coordinates decoded from each state's clut field, then sha256
palettes_are_identical.B08 palette sha256[:16]: e00991475d086313 in LEVEL01, LEVEL08, LEVEL13, LEVEL06

measurements.visual_check: gpu.decodeTexture PNGs from LEVEL06 and LEVEL13 are the same image in both cases: B06 = a small round twinkle sprite (tinted gold at draw time by the FF/C0/00 modulation), B08 = a larger round bubble sprite drawn with the neutral 0x80 tint under semi-transparent blending. Written to /tmp only, not to the repo.

task4_per_level_asset_dependency.practical_consequence: For a mod, moving these plants into any level requires NO new asset beyond the plant body model that phase4_b06_b08_powerups.json already pins (PLANTS/PLANT07.ALL for B06, PLANT06.ALL for B08). The token sprite itself follows the common sprite bank and is rebound automatically. Conversely, editing descriptor 0x80081EF8 / 0x8008203C in the EXE changes the pickup in EVERY level at once.

descriptor_indices_consumed_by_contact_o.method: read the u16 at metaB+0x00 for ctor rows 0..128 in the pristine EXE and collect the distinct action ids; each such action id is a live index into 0x80096B98

collision_with_the_repurpose_list.0x2E: used by ctor 0x1F -- this is OUR B08 bubble

descriptor_indices_consumed_by_contact_o.caveat: the row count 129 is INFERRED from table adjacency (0x8007941C .. 0x80079E30 is exactly 129 * 0x14). Live evidence only proves >= 114 rows are real (ctor 0x71 was observed). Action ids 0, 1, 122 and 123 fall outside the walker's bound (the dispatch tests (action-2) unsigned < 117), so those rows are either unused or handled elsewhere; action id 0 is also the renderer's explicit 'do not draw' value.

unresolved.question: Which function writes descriptor +0x04 (tpage) and +0x06 (clut) at level load, and from what source?
unresolved.what_was_tried: static: an abstract-interpreter scan over the whole resident text found no store into 0x80096B98..0x80096C70 and no `sh +4 / sh +6` pair that targets a descriptor (the six such pairs found are all GTE/matrix code). live: armed a WRITE breakpoint on 0x80081EFC and replayed movies/B06_LevelTransition.movie.json (1162 frames) -- the breakpoint never fired and the descriptor was unchanged before and after. That is inconclusive, not negative: the movie is not documented as Interpreter-recorded, so it may have desynced, and its start and end levels may share the same binding.
unresolved.exact_experiment_that_would_resolve_it: On an Interpreter instance, arm `debugger.addBreakpoint {address: 0x80081EFC, type: 'write'}` AND `{address: 0x80082040, type: 'write'}` BEFORE a genuine level load, then drive a from-boot movie (e.g. movies/flik_to_level01_stall) through the load. Read the halting PC, then pc-4, and the base register; the base will be the 0x80096B98 entry and the source will identify the bank descriptor. A cheaper variant: `accessLog.addWatch` on the same 4 bytes across the same boot, since non-halting instrumentation is free on an Interpreter-recorded movie.
